key_insight: The paper combines large language models with fuzzy logic rules to make disease diagnosis more explainable, auditable, and formally verifiable.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinicians review AI-generated diagnoses with transparent reasoning paths that can be checked against clinical guidelines and adjusted with feedback.
method: LLM extracts medical entities, temporal relations, and fuzzy symptom patterns from patient narratives and guidelines.
These outputs are converted into a symbolic knowledge base using fuzzy logic and declarative rules.
A two-stage process performs symbolic generalization and logic-based verification to produce diagnoses and auditable inference chains.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on public benchmarks and showed performance comparable to state-of-the-art LLMs, while also producing interpretable and formally verifiable diagnostic reasoning.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate extraction and rule design, so errors or bias in the LLM or symbolic rules could still affect diagnosis quality.
paper_title: Uncertainty Reasoning with Large Language Models for Explainable Disease Diagnosis
